Profile the residual scale

Source: R/sigma.R
profile_sigma.Rd

The residual scale is not a nuisance that can be set aside: it enters every class likelihood, and a smaller value sharpens them all, making the Bayes factors more extreme and the responsibilities more confident. The gate is then fitted against something closer to a hard label, which attenuates its coefficient. Estimating the scale with the weights, rather than fixing it, is what keeps that from being an analyst's choice.

Usage

profile_sigma(
  obs,
  candidates,
  trajectory,
  sigma_grid,
  lambda = 1,
  lags = NULL,
  lag_prior = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

obs, candidates, trajectory

As in trajectory_loglik().

sigma_grid

Values of the residual scale to profile over.

lambda

Entropy penalty passed to fit_bank().

lags, lag_prior

Optional lag integration, as in trajectory_loglik().

...

Further arguments to fit_bank().

Value

A list with the profile data frame (sigma and objective), the maximising sigma, and the bank fitted there.

Details

For each value on the grid the bank is refitted and its attained objective recorded, giving a profile whose maximiser is the jointly estimated scale.

See also

fit_bank()

Examples

set.seed(1)
obs <- data.frame(id = rep(1:8, each = 3), time = rep(c(1, 4, 9), 8),
                  value = pmax(rlnorm(24, log(200), 1), 1))
cand <- data.frame(peak = c(100, 300, 900), rate = c(.1, .2, .3))
decay <- function(t, th) th$peak * exp(-th$rate * t)
profile_sigma(obs, cand, decay, sigma_grid = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.8))$sigma
#> [1] 0.5
